title: The role of upper ocean stratification in resurgent marine heatwaves in the East/Japan Sea
abstract: The East/Japan Sea (EJS) has experienced increasingly frequent and intense marine heatwaves (MHWs) in recent years, characterized by prolonged periods of record-breaking sea surface temperatures (SSTs). This study investigates the two most severe MHW events in the EJS during recent summers—2021 and 2023—highlighting the resurgent nature of the 2023 event in contrast to the 2021 MHW, and exploring key differences in the regional coupled ocean–atmosphere system, including the mixed-layer heat budget and various oceanic and atmospheric processes influencing MHW evolution. In both years, the MHWs weakened in mid-August following typhoon passage; however, their subsequent evolution diverged markedly. The 2023 event developed into a resurgent MHW, recovering rapidly after temporary cooling and persisting for nearly three months. This resurgence was facilitated by favorable oceanic preconditioning—rapid shoaling of the mixed layer due to weak wind stress and enhanced stratification—which effectively trapped anomalous heat within the upper ocean, producing a sustained ocean heat-trapping effect. On the atmospheric side, the westward expansion of the Western North Pacific Subtropical High maintained persistent southerly winds that advected warm, moist air into the EJS. The resulting increase in extreme atmospheric humidity from the surface to the upper troposphere further reinforced SST anomalies by suppressing latent heat release from the ocean surface. The coupled feedback between the ocean and atmosphere generated a synergistic double heat-trapping effect that played a key role in sustaining the 2023 MHW. In contrast, although a high-pressure system was also present in 2021, stronger vertical ocean mixing during and after typhoon passage induced upper-ocean cooling, preventing MHW recovery. These findings underscore the crucial role of upper-ocean stratification in controlling MHW duration and recovery, offering new insights into the mechanisms governing extreme ocean temperature events in the EJS.
problem: This paper addresses why atmospheric forcing alone fails to explain the resurgence of some marine heatwaves after cooling, a challenge highlighting the poorly understood but critical role of upper-ocean stratification in controlling heatwave persistence and recovery.
method: This study employs a mixed-layer heat budget analysis to investigate the key oceanic and atmospheric processes, particularly upper-ocean stratification, that controlled the evolution and resurgent nature of recent marine heatwaves in the East/Japan Sea.
task: The task is to investigate the role of upper-ocean stratification in driving the prolonged, resurgent 2023 marine heatwave in the East/Japan Sea by contrasting its oceanic and atmospheric mechanisms with the shorter-lived 2021 event.
innovation: This paper identifies a synergistic “double heat-trapping” mechanism, where strong upper-ocean stratification and high atmospheric humidity combined to sustain the prolonged, resurgent 2023 marine heatwave in the East/Japan Sea.

During the second cooling period, Typhoon Lan passed over the EJS, but wind-speed anomalies remained relatively weak, resulting in only modest deepening of the mixed layer. Once the mixed layer rapidly shoaled afterward, the MHW recovered quickly and subsequently persisted into September (Fig. 3a).

Meanwhile, when intense ocean warming occurred prior to the MHW decay in 2021, both atmospheric and oceanic conditions were favorable for the formation and development of the event. In summer 2021, an anomalous northward shifting of the East Korea Warm Current (EKWC) due to large meandering was observed, which was co-located with the strongest SST anomaly on the western side of the EJS, near the Korean Peninsula (KP) (Fig. 1e)20. This altered EKWC pathway modified regional heat transport and promoted heat convergence along its western flank, favoring localized heat accumulation and thereby limiting the basin-wide expansion of the MHW in 2021. By contrast, in 2023, an eastward-shifted and more coherently oriented current pathway, together with a basin-scale stratified upper-ocean state and an enhanced thermocline gradient, facilitated broader heat redistribution across the central and eastern EJS, allowing the MHW to expand spatially and persist over a much larger area (Fig. S1).

variables—such as temperature, salinity, current components, and sea surface height (SSH)—were obtained from the GLORYS12V1 reanalysis provided by the Copernicus Marine Environment Monitoring Service, with a horizontal resolution of 1/12° and 50 vertical layers. Climatology was derived by smoothing the daily values into monthly resolution over the reference period 1993–2020. Atmospheric variables, including 10-m wind speed, surface net solar and thermal radiation, surface latent and sensible heat fluxes, and mean sea level pressure (MSLP), were obtained from the ERA5 reanalysis dataset22, available at hourly intervals and a horizontal resolution of 0.25° x 0.25°.
